B. Is this measure already running in City of Helsinki (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Same-day chest X-ray report with immediate CT. A radiologist or reporting radiographer reads primary-care chest X-rays while the patient waits; if suspicious, CT is done the same day or within days and the referral is triggered by radiology.
effect_summary_en: In a London randomised trial, immediate chest X-ray reporting gave a median of 32 days from X-ray to lung cancer diagnosis, against 63 days with standard reporting (p=0.03), a saving of 31 days.
supported_en: A 2023 randomised trial in Thorax found the median time from chest X-ray to diagnosis fell from 63 to 32 days with immediate reporting.
not_supported_en: The result comes from one small trial at one London hospital, with 49 cancers and no confidence interval, so the effect in Finland is not shown.
in_use_summary_en: Two extra searches found no public sign of same-day chest X-ray reporting or radiology-triggered CT in Helsinki or HUS; HUS's pathway page says the primary-care doctor makes the referral.
summary_en: No public page shows same-day chest X-ray reporting with immediate CT in Helsinki or HUS. HUS's pathway page says the primary-care doctor sends a referral to HUS's lung disease clinic when an X-ray raises suspicion. A 2023 randomised trial in Thorax (London) cut the median time from chest X-ray to diagnosis from 63 to 32 days.
unanswered_en: I found no page on how fast HUS radiology reports primary-care chest X-rays or whether radiology can order the CT itself.
